episode.title: Resume sessions using the latest persisted provider route instead of a stale billing identity
episode.before: At parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe, the Desktop/TUI resume reader independently extracted provider, base_url, and api_mode only from top-level model_config fields, then fell back to billing_provider. It did not inspect model_config.gateway_runtime, even though the messaging gateway persisted its latest per-turn route there. Consequently, a session whose provider changed after its first accounted call could resume with the current stored model combined with the first-call billing_provider, while stale top-level route fields could also override the newer nested route.
episode.after: At 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480, Desktop/TUI resume delegates route extraction to SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime, the canonical reader already used by CLI resume. That reader gives a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime first precedence, otherwise retains top-level provider/base_url/api_mode, and fills only a missing top-level provider from a routable billing_provider. Resume therefore uses the latest persisted provider/wire tuple while preserving compatibility for older rows containing top-level endpoint fields plus billing_provider.
episode.diff: The change removes the Desktop/TUI reader's hand-written provider and endpoint extraction and replaces it with a call to the shared session-route reader. It also changes the shared reader's legacy fallback from returning top-level fields immediately to augmenting those fields with billing_provider only when provider is absent. Two regression tests cover nested gateway_runtime winning over a stale first-call billing_provider and over stale top-level route keys; 33 lines were added and 24 removed across hermes_state_gateway.py, tui_gateway/server.py, and the focused test file.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 33c6ab002d1fac653d7e772025ef7aaab7c83480 has parent 7fd2f574132fcf8aea71ca485ca489c367fedffe and identifies the defect as Desktop/TUI ignoring nested gateway_runtime and falling back to a billing_provider frozen at the first accounted call.
The messaging gateway persists the current model route as model_config.gateway_runtime, replacing that nested object with the current provider, base_url, and api_mode values.

In the parent, _stored_session_runtime_overrides read top-level model_config provider/base_url/api_mode and used billing_provider when the top-level provider was missing; it had no gateway_runtime lookup.

The changed Desktop/TUI resume reader calls SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime(row) and derives provider, base_url, and api_mode from that returned route, while continuing to read unrelated service-tier and reasoning settings from model_config.
SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime returns a provider-bearing nested gateway_runtime before other representations and filters None values from that nested route.

The shared reader was changed so routable billing_provider fills a missing provider in the top-level route via setdefault instead of being considered only after an immediate top-level return; bare billing buckets remain excluded.

CLI stored_session_route also obtains persisted provider, base_url, and api_mode through SessionDB.session_gateway_runtime, demonstrating that the changed Desktop/TUI path now shares the same route-resolution boundary as CLI resume.

test_resume_honors_gateway_runtime_over_first_call_billing_provider constructs a row with billing_provider anthropic and nested gateway_runtime for openai-codex/codex_responses, then asserts both Desktop/TUI and CLI readers restore the nested route.

test_resume_prefers_gateway_runtime_over_stale_top_level_keys constructs conflicting top-level and nested routes and asserts Desktop/TUI restores the nested provider and wire mode rather than the stale top-level endpoint.

The pre-existing parameterized test continues to assert that a stored provider switch drops an endpoint and wire mode belonging to the previous provider, covering compatibility with older and gateway-written rows.
The commit records both new tests as red on the base with the stale anthropic route and green on the implementation commit.
The implementation changes exactly three files, with 33 insertions and 24 deletions: the shared route reader, the Desktop/TUI consumer, and focused resume regression tests.
The diff between the pinned parent and implementation commit passes git diff --check.

candidate_atomics.name: resolve-persisted-route-by-freshness
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize multiple persisted route representations into one provider/endpoint/wire tuple using explicit freshness precedence: the latest nested runtime route first, then legacy top-level fields, with a routable billing identity only filling a missing provider.

semantic_action.intent: Restore a resumed session on the provider interface most recently used by that session without discarding compatible legacy route metadata.
semantic_action.pre_state: Session metadata may contain a newer nested runtime route, older top-level provider/endpoint fields, and a first-call billing identity that disagree or are only partially populated.
semantic_action.post_state: A provider-bearing nested runtime route wins; otherwise top-level route fields are retained and a routable billing identity fills only a missing provider, while unroutable bare billing buckets do not become route identities.
semantic_action.validation: Conflicting nested-versus-billing and nested-versus-top-level fixtures must resolve to the nested provider and wire mode, while the existing legacy switched-provider fixture must still discard an endpoint belonging to the previous provider.

candidate_atomics.name: delegate-resume-consumer-to-canonical-route-reader
candidate_atomics.description: Replace a consumer-specific reconstruction of persisted provider metadata with the canonical session-route resolver before applying existing endpoint-safety and provider-healing logic.

semantic_action.intent: Keep separate resume surfaces from interpreting the same persisted provider interface differently.
semantic_action.pre_state: One resume surface manually reads only legacy top-level fields and billing identity, while another uses the canonical reader that understands the latest nested runtime route.
semantic_action.post_state: The resume surface obtains provider, endpoint, and wire mode from the canonical resolver, while its existing model restoration, foreign-endpoint rejection, provider healing, reasoning, and service-tier behavior remains downstream.
semantic_action.validation: The focused regression tests assert that Desktop/TUI and CLI select the same nested route for a stale-billing row, and that Desktop/TUI gives the nested route precedence over stale top-level keys.

candidate_workflows.name: adapt-session-resume-to-a-versioned-provider-route
candidate_workflows.description: Establish one precedence-aware interpretation of persisted provider-interface state, then make each resume consumer delegate route extraction to it and validate conflicts between new and legacy representations.

workflow_graph.goal: Resume a session using its latest persisted provider, endpoint, and wire protocol without regressing compatible legacy rows or existing endpoint-safety rules.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A producer persists the latest route in a nested runtime object, but at least one consumer independently reconstructs the route from older top-level fields and a potentially stale billing identity.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Persisted route precedence is centralized and all relevant resume consumers use it; conflicting-representation tests select the latest nested route and legacy endpoint-safety coverage remains intact.
unresolved_or_deferred: No cross-repository resolution pattern is proposed from this single workflow.
